executive_summary: Ran a live, end-to-end acceptance battery (real HybridRetriever + real LLMGenerator + real local Ollama llama3 generation, no mocks) across 17 test categories: 67 total live generation calls (31 main battery + 36 security battery). Full Team4B pytest suite re-run: 1302 passed, 3 skipped, 1 known pre-existing failure, identical to historical baseline, no regression. Core grounding, citation accuracy, fresh-session honesty, OOS refusal, and workspace/document isolation are all strong and reproducible. Two real gaps confirmed live: (1) a narrow but genuine FULL-severity prompt-injection pattern ('forced fixed-output' phrasing) achieves complete output hijacking in 5 of 31 injection cases (~16%), unchanged from Phase 5F/G's prior characterization; (2) Hindi retrieval is phrasing-fragile - two independent live cases show a correctly-answerable Hindi query missing its own known-good content when phrased slightly differently, though generation responded safely (honest decline) in both cases. A secondary pattern - confident narration of wrong-domain retrieved content instead of declining - is also reproduced, matching Phase 5D/5E's original Finding A.

hindi_retrieval_fragility.test: direct live comparison of exact Phase 5I-A ground-truth query 'मल्टी प्रोग्रामिंग ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम क्या होता है?' (spaced compound) vs natural paraphrase 'मल्टीप्रोग्रामिंग क्या है?' (unspaced compound) against identical live HybridRetriever
hindi_retrieval_fragility.result: original phrasing retrieves target chunk at rank 1 (score 0.896); paraphrase does not retrieve it in top 100 at all
hindi_retrieval_fragility.root_cause: default_tokenizer's regex-based Devanagari tokenization treats spaced vs unspaced compound forms as completely disjoint tokens with zero lexical overlap - a BM25 token-boundary sensitivity with no English equivalent for this case
hindi_retrieval_fragility.novelty: distinct from Phase 5I-B/C's cross-script findings - this is a same-script (Hindi->Hindi) phrasing-sensitivity issue, newly characterized this phase

irrelevant_context_narration.test: direct metadata inspection of IRR-02's retrieved chunks
irrelevant_context_narration.result: retrieval was correctly scoped (100% of chunks belonged to the actually-queried workspace); failure is purely in LLM's own reasoning
irrelevant_context_narration.root_cause: model treats 'preemptive'/'schedule' as sufficient lexical grounds to construct an answer rather than recognizing conceptual domain mismatch (CPU scheduling vs transaction scheduling)
irrelevant_context_narration.attribution: model behavior, not retrieval or prompt-construction defect; same root cause as Phase 5D/5E's Finding A, unresolved because no subsequent phase (5F-5I-C) targeted this specific failure mode

prompt_injection_full_severity.root_cause: _neutralize_untrusted_text()'s regex-based defense targets known role-marker/reserved-header strings; it cannot (without an LLM-level intent classifier or architecture change) prevent the underlying LLM from semantically recognizing and complying with a short, unambiguous, fully-formed imperative sentence embedded in retrieved text
prompt_injection_full_severity.attribution: fundamental limitation of prompt-level defenses against instruction-following models, not a Team4B implementation bug; already established Phase 5F/G, reconfirmed live this phase on unmodified code

known_limitations: Prompt injection 'forced fixed-output' pattern (FULL severity, 5/31 live cases): short absolute directive in retrieved content can fully hijack output, especially with no competing genuine content or when phrased in Devanagari Hindi. Known since Phase 5F/G, no complete fix without further architecture intervention. Requires attacker content already indexed (ingestion-side precondition).

Hindi retrieval is phrasing-sensitive including same-script (Hindi->Hindi) cases - compound-word spacing variations can cause complete retrieval miss. New, narrower finding than Phase 5I-B/C's cross-script gap.
Cross-script retrieval (Hinglish/English<->Hindi) remains weaker, per Phase 5I-B/C's established, unresolved findings - not re-tested this phase.

Irrelevant-context narration: LLM occasionally answers using lexically-adjacent-but-wrong-domain content instead of declining (1/4 tested this phase). Bounded - never observed to leak cross-workspace data.
Generation latency is CPU-bound and slow (30-140s/request in this environment) - infrastructure characteristic, not a code defect, relevant for Team4C UX expectations.
Document-isolation test coverage gap - insufficient distinct document_ids in sampled workspace to construct a live test this phase.
MP4/video-upload content does not exist as a distinct source type in either Qdrant collection today - only pdf and youtube. Video acceptance only evidenced via YouTube transcripts.
team4b_readiness_decision: C - TARGETED FIX REQUIRED, scoped specifically and narrowly to the prompt-injection 'forced fixed-output' pattern. Every other dimension tested (grounding, citation integrity, fresh-session honesty, OOS refusal, workspace/document isolation, generalized subject handling, regression stability) is at a B (READY WITH DOCUMENTED LIMITATIONS) level. The one dimension preventing an unqualified READY call is a FULL-severity, reproducible, live-confirmed security gap affecting ~16% of tested injection cases with no proven mitigation. Not a new discovery (Phase 5F/G already found and accepted this residual risk), but its severity (complete output control) and realistic precondition (any indexed document, including potentially compromised course material) mean it should not be silently folded into a documented limitation alongside lower-severity items. No fix implemented this phase - none proven safe and generalized.
recommended_next_step: Escalate the prompt-injection 'forced fixed-output' pattern to the architecture authority (ChatGPT) for a design-level decision - explicitly out of scope for a prompt-level patch per Phase 5F/G's own conclusion. Candidate directions (NOT validated or implemented this phase): output-side heuristic/guardrail flagging suspiciously short question-unrelated answers for re-generation or decline; or an ingestion-side scan for known injection-marker patterns before indexing (a Team4A boundary question).

Once a specific evidence-backed fix is designed, re-run this exact 31-case injection battery (harness preserved and reusable) to measure before/after severity distribution before any production change.

Track the Hindi phrasing-sensitivity finding alongside the already-documented cross-script limitation for a future dedicated Hindi-retrieval-quality phase - not attempted ad hoc here, per Phase 5I-C's explicit instruction not to repeat retrieval-side experiments without new evidence.

If the architecture authority judges the injection risk acceptable given Team4A's actual ingestion trust model (e.g. instructor-only uploads vs open public content), Team4B's classification could be revised to B - READY WITH DOCUMENTED LIMITATIONS without further Team4B code change - deferred to that authority, not decided unilaterally here.
